---
title: "FAQ"
---

## Does this contradict Johnson–Lindenstrauss?

No. JL bounds each distance relative to itself. The paper studies smaller
centered variations and joint decisions not separately controlled by that bound.

## Is `sqrt(m/d)` the correlation achieved by my estimator?

It is a decoder-free ceiling in the isotropic Gaussian model. A particular
estimator can be worse. The centered projected norm attains it for the distance
value in that model.

## Can I apply the nearest-neighbor formula to millions of candidates?

Not without additional analysis. The plurality law is a fixed-`q` limit. Use
the real-data audit and a production-scale retrieval evaluation for growing `q`.

## Why does `audit` disagree with the prediction?

The prediction assumes isotropic Gaussian structure. Clusters, anisotropy,
heavy tails, manifolds, duplicates, and low intrinsic dimension can all change
the answer. The reported spectrum diagnostics help identify the first layer.

## Why not just whiten everything?

For a known noiseless map, row whitening removes reversible output distortion.
It cannot recover discarded directions, and with additive noise small singular
directions remain unstable.

## Which artifact is authoritative?

Source and experiments live here. The paper repository pins a submodule commit
and retains generated publication PDFs/LaTeX. A reproduction manifest hashes
every generated companion artifact.
